questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.category: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers :: Organic Reaction Pathway (Type 1)
questions.question: In [Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers], phenol is treated with chloroform and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ at $60^\circ\text{C}$ (Reimer-Tiemann condition) to form an intermediate that on acidification yields salicylaldehyde $[A]$. When $[A]$ is distilled with zinc dust, what is the major organic compound obtained?
questions.solution: The Reimer-Tiemann reaction introduces an ortho-formyl $(-\text{CHO})$ group to yield salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). Heating with zinc dust selectively reduces the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group to $-\text{H}$ while preserving the formyl group, yielding benzaldehyde.
questions.explanation: Deduce using established organic reaction mechanisms in Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.category: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers :: Stoichiometric Reaction Calculation
questions.question: In [Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers], one mole of glycerol $(\text{CH}_2\text{OH}-\text{CHOH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH})$ reacts completely with excess periodic acid $(\text{HIO}_4)$. How many moles of formaldehyde $(\text{HCHO})$ are formed?
questions.solution: Periodic acid cleaves vicinal diols. Cleavage of the two $\text{C-C}$ bonds consumes $2\text{ moles of }\text{HIO}_4$ to yield $2\text{ moles of }\text{HCHO}$ from the terminal carbons and $1\text{ mole of }\text{HCOOH}$ from the central carbon.
questions.explanation: Solve using reaction stoichiometry in Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers.
